core.title: Plan concurrent journey branches only with explicit fan-out, release, join and failure semantics
core.given: A plan introduces or changes concurrency: parallel journey branches or within-wagon concurrency, or its evidence
core.when: the planner authors the topology, wagons, acceptances or docs for it
core.then: Plan branches as concurrent only if the topology explicitly specifies fan-out, dependency release, join, and failure semantics; otherwise keep them sequential.
prefer: Concurrency only for independent expensive operations whose measured saving exceeds its overhead.
Prove bounded concurrency, prerequisite satisfaction, joining, cancellation, failures and result equivalence; benchmark latency.
avoid: Treating multiple incoming continuations as a join.
More than one outgoing continuation or terminal per route; assuming journeys give fork/join.
Fan-out/fan-in spanning scopes the plan platform does not support crossing.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration or a new runtime dispatch option from this pattern.
core.why: Journeys allow one continuation or terminal per route and lack fork/join, so unspecified parallelism is unsynchronized and unverifiable. Within-wagon concurrency can honor existing contracts.
evidence: Proof of bounded concurrency, prerequisite satisfaction, joining, cancellation, failure handling and result equivalence.
A latency benchmark shows the measured saving exceeds concurrency overhead.
Topology names fan-out, dependency release, join and failure semantics explicitly; the stack's existing plan and source validators pass.
verification: Advisory guidance for agents (severity 3, advisory disposition), not independent enforcement or a new runtime dispatch option; the stack's existing plan and source validators apply.

A check flags plan artifacts where a step with multiple incoming continuations is relied on as a join, routes with more than one outgoing continuation or terminal, and fan-out/fan-in spanning scopes the plan platform does not support crossing.
Concurrency planned inside a single wagon stays within the current runtime boundary and can honor existing contracts; the check does not flag it as out of bounds.

values: journey topology adds parallel branches or a join
operations independent and expensive; measured saving exceeds concurrency overhead

fires: A planner proposes running two independent expensive journey operations in parallel to cut latency.
A journey draft routes several continuations into one step and treats it as a synchronization point.
A plan proposes fan-out/fan-in across scopes the plan platform does not support crossing.
A wagon plan introduces concurrency inside the wagon.

A planner edits acceptances or docs that prove (or omit) bounded concurrency, joining, cancellation, failures, result equivalence or latency for concurrent branches, even if branch structure is unchanged.
doesNotFire: A purely sequential journey with one outgoing continuation or terminal per route and no concurrency planned anywhere in it.
Editing journey wording unrelated to concurrency, joins or their evidence.

neutralityNotes: Journey, wagon, continuation, route and acceptance are treated as the shared ATDD plan-artifact model (they occur in the closed profile vocabulary as roles/artifacts), so the core retains them; they are not stack mechanics. Only 'interlocking' has no neutral counterpart: avoid[2] and verifier_detail[1] keep a generalized unsupported-crossing form in the core with the concrete scope Bun-only, and the third fires example is generalized in place ('across scopes the plan platform does not support crossing'). Per-rule severity 3 / advisory disposition live in core.verification, not the profile. Activation fact notes (observer details for needs_new_observer) are realization notes and are represented only by the observability flag. No profile key was missing: the core needs only the concrete plan-artifact kinds, so proposedKeys is empty.
